title: A simple method for mitochondrial respiration and calcium uptake assessment in pollen tubes
author: Ortiz-Jiménez, López-Aquino, et al.
materials: 22 Start recording baseline fluorescence for 500 s.

steps.title: Prepare PG buffer tube
steps.instruction: Fill a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube with 1.0 mL PG buffer.

steps.title: Collect and de‑petalize flowers
steps.instruction: Select recently flourished flowers and peel off the petals using scissors and tweezers.

steps.title: Transfer anthers to buffer
steps.instruction: Dip the anthers into the Eppendorf tube containing PG buffer.

steps.title: Release pollen grains
steps.instruction: Mildly shake the anthers to release pollen grains into the PG buffer.

steps.title: Germinate pollen tubes
steps.instruction: Close the tube, place it on an orbital shaker set to 60 rpm and 28 °C, and incubate for 2 h.

steps.title: Count pollen tubes
steps.instruction: Pipette 20 μL of the suspension into the hematocytometer sample port and determine cell count by multiplying by the chamber’s predetermined factor.

steps.title: Wash pollen tubes
steps.instruction: Wash the pollen tubes twice with 1 mL PTA buffer by centrifuging at 3000 rpm for 20 s each wash.

steps.title: Calibrate oxygraph
steps.instruction: Calibrate the Liquid‑Phase Hansatech Oxygraph Plus System according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Load pollen tubes into oxygraph
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed pollen tubes to a final concentration of 1 × 10^6 tubes in 0.5 mL PTA buffer containing 10 mM sodium succinate, 0.01 % digitonin and 200 μM ADP, and transfer the suspension into the Oxygraph’s water‑jacketed chamber.

steps.title: Seal oxygraph chamber
steps.instruction: Close the chamber with the supplied plug and verify that no air bubbles remain inside.

steps.title: Permeabilize tubes
steps.instruction: Allow the suspension to stand for 5 min to achieve efficient pollen‑tube permeabilization and baseline stabilization.

steps.title: Measure state 3 respiration
steps.instruction: Record the oxygen consumption rate for 1–2 min (state 3).

steps.title: Measure state 4 respiration
steps.instruction: Inject 2 μg oligomycin and record the oxygen consumption rate for 1–2 min (state 4).

steps.title: Calculate RCR
steps.instruction: Compute the Respiratory Control Ratio (RCR) by dividing the state 3 rate by the state 4 rate.

steps.title: Inhibit mitochondrial respiration
steps.instruction: Add 100 μM potassium cyanide (KCN) and 500 μM salicylhydroxamic acid (SHAM) to the chamber.

steps.title: Prepare calcium assay suspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pollen tubes in PTA buffer containing 10 mM sodium succinate, 0.01 % digitonin, 20 μM EDTA and 2 μM Calcium Green‑5N.

steps.title: Place suspension in fluorimeter
steps.instruction: Transfer the suspension to a cuvette placed in the fluorimeter, stir gently at 60 rpm, ensuring the cuvette port is centered on the magnetic stirrer for laminar flow.

steps.title: Power and connect fluorimeter
steps.instruction: Turn on the mini fluorimeter and connect it via Bluetooth® or USB cable.

steps.title: Configure Logger Pro fluorescence
steps.instruction: Open Logger Pro, select ‘500 nm fluorescence mode’ under the SpectroVis plus sensor configuration.

steps.title: Set acquisition parameters
steps.instruction: Choose the 530 nm acquisition box and ‘Absorbance versus time’, set data collection to 1 sample/second, and set an acquisition interval (e.g., 2000 s).

steps.title: Record baseline fluorescence
steps.instruction: Start recording baseline fluorescence for 500 s.

steps.title: Add calcium pulse
steps.instruction: Add the desired amount of calcium (a pulse around 50 μM is a typical starting point).

steps.title: Measure calcium transport
steps.instruction: Continue recording for at least 2000 s, then save the data.

steps.title: Negative control with RuR
steps.instruction: Start a new trace and repeat the measurement in the presence of freshly prepared 100 nM ruthenium red (RuR); note that a 100 μM RuR stock solution must be freshly made.

steps.title: Perform replicates and analyze
steps.instruction: Carry out the required biological replicates and quantify calcium transport rates (fold changes) in arbitrary units using Logger Pro® or Excel®.

description: In order to test the method, pollen grains were isolated from mature flowers (Fig. 1A) hydrated in PG buffer and incubated for 2 h. As expected, pollen tubes emerged and were counted in the Neubauer chamber (Fig. 1B). Cell number was determined and adjusted either for oxygen consumption experiments or calcium transport assessment. Samples were then washed twice in PTA buffer in order to remove excess calcium. Pollen tubes were then permeabilized with 0.01% digitonin or 0.5% DMSO (control) for 5 min and stained with 0.1% Evans Blue solution. As expected, permeabilized pollen tubes were stained with Evans Blue (Fig. 1C). In parallel, a separate batch of pollen tubes were treated with 0.01% digitonin for five minutes inside the oxygraph´s chamber and ADP was added to obtain state 3 respiration (Fig. 2). Oligomycin addition resulted in a transient decrease in respiration typically associated with ADP phosphorylation blockade (Fig. 2A). Furthermore, addition of 100 μM KCN significantly decreased state 3 respiration whereas subsequent addition of 500 μM SHAM resulted in no significant changes when compared with respiration in the presence of cyanide (Fig. 2B).Fig. 1Pollen tube germination (A,B) and plasmalemma permeabilization assessment (C). Pollen tubes were allowed to grow for 2 h, the cells were counted and permeabilized with 0.01% digitonin or 0.5% DMSO. Plasma membrane permeabilization was then assessed by staining with 0.1% Evans Blue. Representative experiments n = 4.Fig. 1Fig. 2In situ monitoring of oligomycin-sensitive respiration (A), CN- and SHAM-sensitive respiration (B) and RuR-sensitive calcium transport activity in permeabilized pollen tubes (C). Permeabilized pollen tubes were resuspended inside the oxygraph’s reaction chamber and state 3 respiration was measured. State 4 respiration was then assessed by adding 2 μg oligomycin (A).
